Text 1
An economist argues that when a city raises its minimum wage, businesses respond by hiring fewer workers, so overall employment falls.

Text 2
Researchers compared restaurants in two neighboring areas, one of which had just raised its minimum wage. Employment at restaurants in the area with the higher wage did not fall compared with the other area; if anything, it rose slightly.
stem: Based on the texts, the researchers in Text 2 would most likely characterize the economist's argument in Text 1 as ______
choices: not supported by what they observed when comparing the two neighboring areas.
confirmed by the slight rise in employment found in the area with the higher wage.
correct for restaurants but probably incorrect for most other kinds of businesses.
impossible to test, since no two areas can ever be compared in a fair way.
steps: Text 1 predicts employment falls when the minimum wage rises.
Text 2 found no fall (a slight rise) where the wage went up.
So their findings don't support the prediction.
A rise doesn't confirm a predicted fall; Text 2 studied only restaurants; and the researchers did compare the areas.
key: Characterize the claim using the evidence Text 2 actually presents, without overstating it.
